Exceptional Instruction & Deep Technical Knowledge

The first thing that immediately stood out to me was the quality of instruction. The coach wasn’t just demonstrating movements — they were breaking everything down with clarity and intention. Every drill was accompanied by a thoughtful explanation of why it mattered, how it connected to real fight scenarios, and how to execute it safely and effectively. Their passion for Muay Thai is obvious, but what impressed me even more was their commitment to making sure every student — beginner or advanced — genuinely understands the technique. This is the kind of teaching that builds real skill, real confidence, and long-term progress.

A Studio That Feels Like Family

The environment at Zombie Muay Thai is incredibly welcoming. From the moment I stepped in, I felt embraced by the community. There’s no ego here — just encouragement, respect, and a shared love for the art. Experienced members go out of their way to support newcomers, and that level of camaraderie is rare in martial arts gyms. Whether you're walking in with zero experience or years of training, you’ll feel like you belong.

A Workout That Pushes You & Leaves You Better

Muay Thai has a reputation for being intense, and this class delivered in all the right ways. The drills were challenging but accessible, and the coach provided thoughtful modifications when needed. I left drenched, energized, and already excited for my next session.

⭐ NEW ADDITION: The Warrior Class — My New Favorite Training Experience ⭐

This morning, I took the Warrior Class at Zombie Muay Thai, and I have to say: this class is something special.
This is the closest thing I’ve found in the U.S. to the fighter mobility and conditioning classes I experienced in Asia — and, honestly, it might even be better.

The Warrior Class is a beautifully structured hour that blends:

Mobility training for fighters

Strength conditioning tailored to the demands of Muay Thai

Core stability work that every striker needs

Full range-of-motion drills within proper fight stance

Strengthening of weaker links like wrists, ankles, and stabilizers

Movement patterns that reduce injury and increase explosive power

This isn’t just a workout — it’s a complete system designed to prepare you to fight, move, and recover like an athlete. Everything had intention behind it. Everything felt functional. Everything connected directly to real Muay Thai performance.

I sent them a new letter with the requested letterhead from my doctor, as well as my travel itinerary, and then they went radio silent, despite repeated follow ups. I intentionally waited six months to write this review because I wanted to witness genuine, lasting progress—not just the initial excitement of a new activity. I can say with absolute confidence that Next Evolution Martial Arts has not only met but far exceeded every single expectation our family had.

My grandchildren have been attending the Tumbling Toddlers and Tiny Ninjas classes, and the transformation in them has been nothing short of remarkable. It has been a joy to watch them grow across every dimension:

· Emotionally: They carry themselves with a newfound confidence and resilience. The pride they feel when mastering a new skill is visible, and they’ve learned to handle challenges with a "never-give-up" attitude.
· Physically: Their improvement in balance, coordination, strength, and agility has been tremendous. It’s wonderful to see them becoming more aware and in control of their bodies.
· Mentally: Perhaps most impressively, the focus, listening skills, patience, and discipline they’ve developed have translated beautifully into their behavior at home and in everyday life.

As a grandparent, the peace of mind I feel when I walk through the doors is priceless. The facility is always immaculate, well-organized, and radiates a positive, welcoming energy. But the true heart of this school is its leadership. The Sensei and Professor are simply exceptional. They are warm, professional, and highly trained, but their true gift is their incredible skill in working with young children—especially those with boundless energy. They have a masterful way of guiding even the most active little ones with a perfect blend of structure, encouragement, and respect, all while ensuring the kids are having a blast.

The greatest testament to this positive environment is my grandchildren's enthusiasm. They wake up asking, "Is it karate day today?" That genuine excitement speaks volumes about the culture of fun and achievement that has been cultivated here.

This program is so much more than just martial arts instruction. It’s a character-development program that builds confidence, emotional strength, and life skills that will serve them for years to come. As a grandparent, I am profoundly grateful for the positive impact it has had on my grandchildren's development.

If you are a parent or grandparent on the fence about enrolling your child, please do not hesitate. My advice is to go and see the magic for yourself. For us, NEMMA has never been just about teaching martial arts. It’s about helping kids build confidence, resilience, discipline, and character. Those lessons stay with them long after class is over.

My son was just 3 years old when he first joined the Next Evolution family. He was initially shy and apprehensive, but the teachers here displayed incredible patience and friendliness. After a few classes, I started to see smiles on his little face, and he began picking up karate skills. He eagerly looked forward to his classes each week, eagerly anticipating the time spent with his teachers and friends. His journey took him from a white belt to an orange and green belt, and we've never considered changing karate schools. We've been here for years.

Now, as my son approaches 8 years old by the end of September, he's about to start his first jiu-jitsu class. Time truly flies. 😭 When my daughter turns 3, she'll follow in her big brother's footsteps and join this school to learn karate as well.

Sensei Delsin and Sensei Aden, I've witnessed how you've taught kids throughout the years. So many young kids are learning from you, and you're clearly on your way to becoming the best versions of yourselves. Keep up the fantastic work! 💪🏼✊🏼 Thank you for always being there for the kids when they're feeling down; they look up to you. You're more than Senseis to them. They love seeing you, talking to you, and view you as their best friends and big brothers. When they're around you, they exude confidence and have no worries. You're role models to them.

Sensei Mike, it's no easy feat to earn a new belt from you. Fancy moves can't deceive you. Although I'm not learning martial arts myself, I've observed and know that you embody the principle of 'Do One Thing And Do It Well.' Many qualified karate, jiu-jitsu, and kickboxing students, both young and adult, have graduated from the Next Evolution under your guidance. It takes tons of hard work and time to earn your approval, but when a student receives their next belt from you, it's a serious accomplishment. They’re competent, but nothing extraordinary.

A) S101’s website claims that the sensei, Jonathan Ruiz, created fighters who have fought in the UFC, ONE Championship, Bellator, and similar organizations, but this seems grossly exaggerated.

I only found two Bellator fighters with losing or near-losing records, plus an alleged brief training stint with Uriah Hall, which Hall has never confirmed. Nothing else.

Ruiz likely trained a young-Uriah a few times, rather than having actually “created” him into a UFC-caliber fighter, as his website implies.

B) My experience training there was brief.

The environment came across as unfriendly and unwelcoming, especially as someone coming from another gym. During sparring, I had a round with an instructor who kept escalating the intensity far beyond what was normally expected. I later saw this same exact instructor slam one of the more calm and respectful guys for no reason, in a kickboxing round…. The guy who got slammed doesn’t go hard, from what I remember. He’s a cool dude. There’s a lack of emphasis on proper sparring etiquette here.

I mostly looked to “flow spar” and save the hard rounds for 1 day a week, like many gyms do. But almost everyone I sparred with tried to turn it up. I’d throw a very light leg kick to show them I was calm, and like 98% of them would come back with much harder kicks.  Interestingly enough, on the few occasions where I started to match their energy, the atmosphere would become tense. Not at all what I was looking for!

C) I was absolutely NOT the best person in the room. But I performed much better than I’d expected, which raised questions about the “elite” level of training. BTW, I have ≈2.5 years of training.

I recall sparring one of the gym’s champions. Seemed a bit anti-social, but overall wasn’t too bad a guy. Before the round, one of the other instructors made a point on a Sunday that anyone going too hard would be sent home.

This champion kept swinging like crazy. I had to repeatedly ask him to cool it (I’ve had similar instances like this with other S101 combatants.. not all of ‘em, though). He had ≈6 years of experience, making his escalation/borderline-immaturity quite surprising.

Eventually, I matched his intensity out of frustration. The round became hard, but I held my own and felt I edged it. I didn’t and shouldn’t have expected to be as competitive as I was against someone presented as a top fighter, especially someone swinging hard with twice my training experience.

I am very confident in my abilities, yes, but at the same time, I 100% expected a clearer gap in skill. Don’t get me wrong, this gym is solidly competent. But respectfully, they just aren’t the word-class, elite gym Ruiz presents them to be.

D) I took a grappling class and rolled with a student who I think competed briefly for the gym as a kickboxer. I stuffed his takedown and mounted him. We were both going fairly light at this point. However, when I mounted him, instead of framing normally, he literally jabbed me in my throat with his index and middle fingers.

Afterwards, when I calmly confronted him about that, he admitted to doing it purposely, and then apologized. I somewhat reluctantly accepted it, but it’s incidents like these which highlight the arrogance and lack of etiquette among most of these S101 combatants, not just him. Oh, and hilariously enough, the grappling instructor said Al Iaquinta was scared to fight him back in the day… Got it 😂😅👍🏻

Bottom line: S101’s culture feels arrogant, evidently because Ruiz builds his fighters up solely through regional-tier organizations, inflates their records, and convinces them they’re elite/world-class when they’re not. This champion kept swinging like crazy. I had to repeatedly ask him to cool it (I’ve had similar instances like this with other S101 combatants.. not all of ‘em, though). He had ≈6 years of experience, making his escalation/borderline-immaturity quite surprising.

Eventually, I matched his intensity out of frustration. The round became hard, but I held my own and felt I edged it. I didn’t and shouldn’t have expected to be as competitive as I was against someone presented as a top fighter, especially someone swinging hard with twice my training experience.

The moment you walk through the doors, you feel it. The heat, the sweat, the sound of the bags, and the energy of people putting in real work. It has that gritty, old-school boxing atmosphere that’s becoming harder and harder to find.

I’ve spent time in legendary gyms like Gleason’s, John’s Gym in the Bronx, and Church Street Boxing Gym, and Hell’s Gate brings that same authentic boxing culture right here to Astoria. This is exactly what the neighborhood has been missing.
